title: Collocations with Take, Give, and Get

sections.title: Collocations with TAKE
sections.content:
Common fixed expressions with TAKE:
• take responsibility — Leaders must take responsibility for their decisions.
• take into account — We need to take all factors into account.
• take advantage of — She took advantage of the free training courses.
• take place — The meeting will take place on Friday.
• take turns — The children took turns reading aloud.

sections.title: Collocations with GIVE and GET
sections.content:
Essential expressions with GIVE and GET:
• give priority to — We must give priority to patient safety.
• give rise to — Inequality gives rise to social unrest.
• give the impression — He gives the impression of being confident.
• get rid of — We need to get rid of old files.
• get the hang of — Once you get the hang of it, driving becomes easy.
• get to grips with — New employees must get to grips with the software quickly.

exercises.question: ___ responsibility means to accept blame or duty:
To consider all relevant factors is to take them into ___:
exercises.explanation: Take into account means to consider something.

exercises.question: To remove something unwanted is to get ___ of it:
exercises.explanation: Get rid of means to remove or dispose of.

exercises.question: 'Give ___ to' means to cause something:
exercises.explanation: Give rise to means to cause or produce.

exercises.question: To learn how to do something new is to get the ___ of it:
exercises.explanation: Get the hang of means to learn how to do something.

exercises.question: The event will take ___ next Monday:
exercises.explanation: Take place means to happen or occur.

exercises.question: To treat something as most important is to give ___ to it:
exercises.explanation: Give priority to means to treat as most important.

exercises.question: To benefit from an opportunity is to take ___ of it:
exercises.explanation: Take advantage of means to make good use of an opportunity.
